logline: Two wildly mismatched detectives - uptight local cop Dulcie and abrasive big-city Eddie - investigate a string of male murders in a Tasmanian festival town, with the comedy landing as hard as the corpses.

renewal.note: Season 2 premiered on Prime Video in March 2026, relocating the action to Darwin. Prime Video confirmed the renewal after Season 1's strong reception.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 23 critics with an 88% audience score. Critics described it as the year's most surprising crime comedy - a perfect fusion of mordant humour and genuine thriller mechanics.

pull_quotes.text: Like Broadchurch mashed with a feminist, less gun-packed Hot Fuzz.
Certainly the funniest crime show, and potentially one of the year's best.

seasons.review_body: Deadloch arrived on Prime Video in June 2023 and immediately earned a rare 100% Rotten Tomatoes score from 23 critics. Created by Kate McCartney and Kate McLennan, the series exploits a genre gap: the murdered-women crime procedural flipped on its axis, with the victims male and the investigators a chaotic female partnership. Kate Box as the methodical local detective Dulcie and Madeleine Sami as the profane, unstoppable Eddie from Darwin form one of streaming's best mismatched-cop pairings. Critics at Slate compared it to a feminist Hot Fuzz; Decider noted it laughs at the investigators rather than the murder. The Tasmanian setting - its parochialism, its passive-aggressiveness, its folk-festival absurdity - functions as a fifth character. AACTA awarded it Best Comedy Series and Best Screenplay.

episode_reviews.title: It Was a Dark and Stormy Night
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the town, the corpse, and the comedy in equal measure. The Dulcie-Eddie dynamic is live from the first scene: two worldviews that are simply incompatible, assigned to the same case.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Eddie's arrival at the crime scene - her reading of the situation versus Dulcie's. Two detectives, one body, zero common ground.

episode_reviews.title: The Night of Living Deadloch
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers on every thread the show laid down - the mystery resolution is both surprising and, in retrospect, inevitable. The comedy and the thriller have been running at different speeds for seven episodes; here they arrive at the same moment.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final confrontation in the festival venue - played for both stakes and satirical absurdity simultaneously.

critic_note.text: You really will be guessing all the way to the end, with unpredictable twists.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 relocated Dulcie and Eddie from Tasmania to Darwin - a broader, hotter, more politically charged canvas. The six-episode run premiered in March 2026 on Prime Video. Critical aggregation is still forming as of this writing; early audience response on the platform tracked favourably. The season introduces Eddie's ex-partner as both victim and complicating factor, adding a personal dimension to the detective dynamic. Verdict to be updated as critical consensus solidifies.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 trades Deadloch's claustrophobic festival-town paranoia for the sprawling heat of Darwin - a tonal shift that widens the show's canvas but loses some of the first season's satirical precision.
